confidence.rationale: The packet’s effective outcome is low_confidence, and reopened primary sources confirm unresolved current-menu coverage, inconsistent live versus recently indexed Toast scope, and no complete allergen or cross-contact disclosure.

confirmedFindings: Reconciliation counts: 16 reconciled, 16 unique reconciled, 0 duplicate reconciled keys; 10 artifact/not_applicable, 2 variant_match/accurately_unavailable, 2 exact_match/verified, and 2 normalized_match/accurately_unavailable.
Bakeshop Falls Church identity and its restaurant-linked Toast ordering catalog are verified.

The official menu hub links a current full-menu document, but that document could not be reopened. This incomplete surface cannot support product-absence findings, negative allergen claims, complete allergen arrays, or cross-contact conclusions.
The official cake page explicitly names cream-cheese icing and Reese’s peanut butter/PB products, supporting narrow restaurant-issued milk and peanut positives at the applicable product level.

The Toast catalog explicitly names ingredients or identities including butter, peanut butter, pecans, almonds, milk, pistachio, egg, cheese, and sesame on selected products. These support only narrow linked-vendor positives for the products where they appear.

The live Toast page currently exposes sweets and drinks, while recently crawled representations of the same catalog also expose breakfast and sandwiches. This temporal inconsistency confirms that Luna’s claim of complete enumeration is unsafe, although it does not conclusively establish that every indexed product is currently orderable.
Multiple frozen rows are headings, slogans, calls to action, or other extraction artifacts rather than independently sellable products.

The substantive scope-incomplete, unresolved-surface, PDF/difficult-extraction, count-drift, non-exact-reconciliation, allergen-mismatch, and low-confidence risks remain valid despite Terra’s incomplete exact gate-ID coverage.
rejectedFindings: Reject any interpretation of the absent cross-contact disclosure as evidence that cross-contact exists or does not exist; it establishes only that cross-contact status is unresolved.
Reject complete allergen arrays or allergen negatives inferred from the cake page, Toast descriptions, or any other incomplete menu surface.

Reject item-specific milk promotion for Gingersnap Cream Pie or Oatmeal Cream Pie when based only on the culinary term “buttercream”; catalog-level milk evidence elsewhere does not transfer to those products.
Reject treating recently indexed breakfast and sandwich content as conclusively live without qualification, because the directly reopened Toast catalog currently omits those categories.

Reject treating the deterministic duplicate-presentation metric as proof of duplicate baseline reconciliation; the packet reports 16 unique reconciled items and zero duplicate reconciled keys. The presentation-level warning remains unresolved and requires structural review.
Reject removal conclusions for Bacon/Ham, DAILYBREAD, or other PDF-derived rows while the current official full-menu document remains unavailable.

additionalEvidence.summary: The official menu hub identifies Falls Church and links the full-menu and cake-menu documents, but does not itself enumerate products or allergens.
Current cake descriptions explicitly name cream-cheese icing and Reese’s peanut butter/PB products, supporting narrow positive ingredient evidence but no complete allergen arrays.

The reopened Falls Church catalog verifies identity and currently shows sweets and drinks with selected explicit ingredient identities; recently crawled versions additionally show breakfast and sandwiches, including an express sesame statement for the New Yorker.
The current full-menu target could not be safely reopened or extracted, leaving its contents unresolved.

summary: Eleven affected baseline items are listed above; reconciliation is 16/16 with 16 unique keys and zero duplicate reconciled keys. Sol upholds the packet’s low_confidence effective outcome. Terra correctly identified incomplete menu and allergen coverage and preserved several valid narrow positives, but its breakfast/sandwich currency claim requires temporal qualification, its cross-contact gate must be understood as unresolved rather than positive evidence, and buttercream alone should not promote item-specific milk claims.
